findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant scoping when fetching documents
findings.body: When a caller supplies another tenant’s document ID, `db.find` now queries only by `documentId`. Because `getDocument` also stops forwarding `ctx.tenantId`, this introduces a cross-tenant authorization bypass wherever document IDs are known or guessable.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve the exported loader contract
findings.body: Existing callers of the exported `loadDocument(db, tenantId, documentId)` API now fail TypeScript compilation due to the removed parameter. JavaScript callers continue running but pass `tenantId` as the document ID, producing an incorrect query.

findings.title: [P2] Keep the exported cache module available
findings.body: Consumers importing `readCached` through the existing `src/cache.ts` module path can no longer resolve that module. Removing the exported module without a replacement or migration path is a breaking contract change.

findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant scoping when querying documents
findings.body:
For a request under tenant A using a document ID belonging to tenant B, the query is now only `{ documentId }`, allowing `db.find` to return tenant B’s document. This removes the existing tenant-isolation boundary and creates cross-tenant data exposure.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Preserve the exported `loadDocument` call contract
findings.body:
Existing TypeScript callers using `loadDocument(db, tenantId, documentId)` now fail with “Expected 2 arguments, but got 3.” JavaScript callers silently bind `tenantId` as `documentId` and query the wrong record.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore the exported cache module
findings.body:
Deleting `src/cache.ts` breaks module resolution for every existing consumer or test importing `readCached` from this module, causing compile-time or runtime “module not found” failures.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant scoping when fetching documents
findings.body:
In a multi-tenant database, an authenticated user can supply another tenant’s document ID and retrieve it because the query no longer includes `ctx.tenantId`. This introduces a cross-tenant authorization bypass/IDOR whenever document IDs are known or guessable.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
